title: Leave room to walk
answer: Keep about 90 cm for main walkways, 60 cm around beds, and 45 cm between a sofa and the coffee table. As a rule, leave roughly 40% of the floor free.

title: Making a small room feel bigger
answer: Use light walls and one floor finish throughout, furniture on legs, a large mirror opposite the window, and fewer, larger pieces instead of many small ones.

title: Layered lighting
answer: Combine three layers: general light (ceiling), task light (reading, cooking) and accent light (lamps, LED strips). Warm white (2700-3000 K) feels homely in living and sleeping areas.

title: Choosing a colour palette
answer: Try 60-30-10: 60% a calm base (walls, floor), 30% a secondary colour (large furniture, textiles), 10% an accent (cushions, art). Test paint samples in morning and evening light.

title: Rug sizes
answer: In a living room, at least the front legs of the sofa and chairs should sit on the rug. Under a dining table, the rug should reach about 60 cm past the table on every side.

title: Pets and children
answer: Choose scratch-resistant floors (porcelain tile, vinyl, hard lacquered wood), washable or performance fabrics, and rounded table edges. Darker, patterned textiles hide wear.

title: Kitchens, bathrooms and structural changes
answer: Kitchen and bathroom layouts depend on water, drainage and electrics, and moving walls may be structural. Ideas in the plan are conceptual: a qualified professional must check them before any work.

title: Mixing styles
answer: Pick one main style for the large pieces and surfaces, and borrow only accents from a second. Repeat each material or colour at least twice in the room so it looks intentional.
